# Salvation Army prepares 5,500 Thanksgiving meals as demand for assistance grows
PUBLISHED 5:19 PM ET Nov. 26, 2026 PUBLISHED 5:19 PM EST Nov. 26, 2026

ORLANDO, Fla. — The Salvation Army partnered with Valencia College and other community organizations to provide thousands of Thanksgiving meals to people across Central Florida Thursday.
The organization prepared 5,500 meals as part of its annual Eric and Diane Holm Thanksgiving Community Meal, but the work behind the holiday feast began months ago.

Valencia College’s School of Management and Culinary Arts began ordering food in June, with students and faculty beginning meal preparations Monday.

About 40 students, faculty, staff and volunteers helped prepare the meals on Thanksgiving Day.
The menu included 1,360 pounds of turkey, 1,632 pounds of mashed potatoes, 1,200 pounds of stuffing, 86 gallons of gravy and 5,500 dinner rolls.

For culinary students, the experience provided an opportunity to develop skills beyond their typical classroom instruction.
The Salvation Army expected approximately 1,500 people to attend its sit-down meal at its gymnasium on West Colonial Drive in Orlando. Another 4,000 meals were designated for delivery through a partnership with The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

Volunteers also planned to deliver meals directly to homeless encampments.
While the number of Thanksgiving meals prepared remained relatively steady compared to last year, Salvation Army Area Commander Major Roger Glick said the organization is seeing a growing need for assistance.

“Our services at the Salvation Army have increased about 40%. So we’re seeing definitely a little more pressure for people needing assistance,” Glick said.

Glick said requests for food, rental and utility assistance have increased, while donations have declined slightly.

![Valencia College Culinary Arts program students Emily Corbett, left, and Yarianlis Delgado, check on sliced turkey platters during early-morning preparation of the 5,500 meals distributed at The Salvation Army Orlando Command’s annual Thanksgiving dinner. In total, culinary students helped prep about 1,300 pounds of turkey, about 1,600 pounds of mashed potatoes and 86 gallons of gravy, which will be sent to the Salvation Army Orlando and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints for their annual Thanksgiving Community Meal.

 BY Bryanna Howard Orlando

ORLANDO, Fla. — The Salvation Army partnered with Valencia College and other community organizations to provide thousands of Thanksgiving meals to people across Central Florida Thursday.

The organization prepared 5,500 meals as part of its annual Eric and Diane Holm Thanksgiving Community Meal, but the work behind the holiday feast began months ago.

Valencia College’s School of Management and Culinary Arts began ordering food in June, with students and faculty beginning meal preparations Monday.

About 40 students, faculty, staff and volunteers helped prepare the meals on Thanksgiving Day.

The menu included 1,360 pounds of turkey, 1,632 pounds of mashed potatoes, 1,200 pounds of stuffing, 86 gallons of gravy and 5,500 dinner rolls.

For culinary students, the experience provided an opportunity to develop skills beyond their typical classroom instruction.

Volunteers also planned to deliver meals directly to homeless encampments.
